step1_analysis.description: A replica bias circuit used in adaptive supply regulation to model the delay of a VCO or buffer stage. It consists of PMOS voltage dividers and an RC load (using a MOSCAP) to emulate the critical path characteristics of the serial link.

paper_reference.title: Adaptive Supply Serial Links With Sub-1-V Operation and Per-Pin Clock Recovery

I_VCO_SUPPLY.description: DC current drawn from the VCO_SUPPLY node.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on square-law estimation for SKY130 PMOS devices with W/L = 5u/0.5u.

V_N1_DC.description: DC voltage at node N1, which acts as a divided voltage reference.

sky130_expected.calculation: Voltage divider between XM3 and (XM1 || XM2). With VCTRL=0.9V, XM2 is mostly off. XM3 and XM1 have identical dimensions and Vg=0, so V(N1) settles around half of VCO_SUPPLY (1.0V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Symmetric PMOS divider with grounded gates.

sky130_expected.calculation: Voltage divider between XM7 and XM6. Both have Vg=0 and identical W/L. V(N0) will be approximately half of ADAPTIVE_SUPPLY (1.0V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Symmetric PMOS divider with grounded gates.

t_delay_N2.description: Transient delay from ADAPTIVE_SUPPLY step to N2, representing the replica RC delay.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_XM4 * C_XM5. C_XM5 is a 5u/0.5u MOSCAP (~12.5fF). R_XM4 is a PMOS in linear region (~10kOhm). Delay ~ 125ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using estimated ON-resistance of XM4 and gate capacitance of XM5.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating points, VCTRL sweep characteristics, and transient step response of the replica bias circuit.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Replica Bias Circuit Testbench

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 GND GND N1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 GND VCTRL N1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 GND VCO_SUPPLY VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N2 GND N0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 GND N2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 GND GND N0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N0 GND ADAPTIVE_SUPPLY VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 GND VDD N0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}

* Voltage Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVCTRL VCTRL 0 0.9
VVCO VCO_SUPPLY 0 1.0
VADAPT ADAPTIVE_SUPPLY 0 pwl(0 0 1n 0 1.1n 1.0)

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
  * 1. DC Operating Point
  op
  let i_vco = -i(VVCO)
  let v_n1_dc = v(N1)
  let v_n0_dc = v(N0)
  print i_vco v_n1_dc v_n0_dc

  * 2. Transient Analysis for Step Response
  tran 10p 5n
  meas tran t_delay_N2 trig v(ADAPTIVE_SUPPLY) val=0.5 rise=1 targ v(N2) val=0.25 rise=1

  * 3. DC Sweep of VCTRL
  dc VVCTRL 0 1.8 0.05
  meas dc v_n1_min min v(N1)
  meas dc v_n1_max max v(N1)

  quit
.endc
.end
